data.title: We Like WDB coco's (TSE:7079) Earnings For More Than Just Statutory Profit
data.description:

A Closer Look At WDB coco's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

For the year to September 2026, WDB coco had an accrual ratio of -0.26. Therefore, its statutory earnings were very significantly less than its free cashflow. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of JP¥938m, well over the JP¥732.0m it reported in profit. WDB coco shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months.

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. data.title: Does Earnings Beat Change The Bull Case For B&M (LSE:BME)?
data.description:
• B&M European Value Retail reported half year sales of £2,848 million and net income of £84 million, and guided for full year core profit to be at or slightly above market expectations.
  • Improved UK like for like sales, a 94 basis point uplift in trading gross margin, and a strategy that prioritises refits over rapid store expansion highlight a shift toward efficiency and cash generation quality.
  • We will now look at how B&M European Value Retail's higher full year profit guidance could reshape the company's broader investment narrative.
Spot similar discount retailers that combine profit guidance upgrades with disciplined cash generation in our hand-picked screener of 6 high quality undiscovered gems.

B&M European Value Retail Investment Narrative Recap

To own B&M European Value Retail, you need to believe it can keep turning its discount model into dependable cash while running a tighter UK estate. The upgraded full year profit guidance leans on better like for like trends and gross margin, so the key near term catalyst remains execution on refits and merchandising across the wider store base.

The biggest operational risk sits around cost pressure and debt, given interest payments are not well covered by earnings. If wage, rent or supply chain expenses increase further, that could squeeze cash generation just as management is trying to prove this new, slower expansion phase can still support the balance sheet.

The half year 2027 results, with sales of £2,848 million and net income of £84 million, are central to the current B&M European Value Retail story. Profit guidance in line with or slightly above market expectations places more emphasis on management’s claim that the refit first approach can support margins, even with fewer UK openings planned.

According to Zer0, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, insider buying from the CEO and other directors has been a key part of the thesis. Zer0 highlights sizeable director purchases over the past two years, which may sharpen attention on execution of the profit upgrade and on whether earnings growth near the forecast 9% a year actually occurs.

Zer0’s narrative lands on a fair value of £1.50 per share for B&M European Value Retail, based on revenue rising 4.1% a year and future profit margins reaching 2.8%, which together are used to frame what they see as a reasonable earnings power for the business.
